info.title: Ordex gateway API
info.summary: Portable Bitcoin orders, verified before you act.
info.description: The HTTP contract an Ordex gateway serves under `/api/ordex`. Amounts and protocol quantities are atomic integers carried as decimal strings, never as floating point numbers. Reads answer 200. Writes answer 201 and are rate limited. Errors use the envelope in `ErrorResponse`. The gateway composes and verifies transactions; it never signs, never holds or contributes funds, and never broadcasts on its own initiative. Version 1.1 adds offers v1 (item, collection, and trait offers with a funded Taproot output, an independent two-signer acceptance path, and a buyer recovery path), ask replacement, and batch purchase. Every 1.0 operation is unchanged.

get.description: Reports configuration completeness and, separately, whether a Bitcoin listing can actually be verified right now: storage writable, both nodes answering, and the ord index within its accepted lag of Bitcoin Core.

get.summary: The protocol contract this gateway speaks
The markets this gateway serves, and what it verifies for each
get.description: Every entry states its verification scope in plain language and its capabilities as booleans. An entry in the catalog never implies a working flow beyond what its capabilities state.
Paging is keyset, never offset. A request carrying an `offset` parameter is refused with 400, and a malformed cursor is a 400 rather than a silent restart from the first page.

parameters.name: protocols
parameters.description: Comma separated catalog ids. Applied before sorting and pagination.

parameters.name: group
parameters.description: A catalog group id, expanded to every protocol it contains.

parameters.name: seller
parameters.description: Restricts the page to the listings one seller script owns.

parameters.name: assetInscriptionId
parameters.description: Restricts the page to orders claiming one inscription. Resolved through an index of order claims.

parameters.name: assetOutpoint
parameters.description: Restricts the page to orders claiming an asset at one `txid:vout`.

parameters.name: sort
parameters.description: Every sort ends on the order id, which is unique, so the ordering is total and a cursor resumes exactly. An unpriced order sorts after every priced one in both price directions.

parameters.name: limit
parameters.description: Page size as a decimal string.

parameters.name: cursor
parameters.description: The keyset resume point a previous page answered with.

get.summary: The appended lifecycle log, newest first
get.description: Reads the appended transition log, so an entry is something that happened rather than a listing's current state restated after the fact.

200.description: The order, without its signed artifact.

get.summary: The signed artifact for one live listing
get.description: Deliberately its own rate limited request. A browse response carrying raw PSBTs would hand every public ask to anything that can read the market. Only a live listing hands over its artifact; any other state is refused with 400.

200.description: The signed artifact and its current verification.

post.summary: Take a signed artifact and verify it
post.description: A source may supply signed order evidence, but it never overrides what the node and the ord index prove. The claims travel as evidence and the authorities decide the state.

post.summary: Take a signed OpenOrdex event and verify it
post.description: Accepts a kind 802 Nostr event carrying a signed PSBT, verifies the event signature, then verifies the order exactly as a direct import.
Composes the one input, one output PSBT a seller signs `SIGHASH_SINGLE | SIGHASH_ANYONECANPAY`. The asset and outpoint are verified against the node and the ord index before anything is composed.

201.description: The unsigned seller half and its inspection.

post.summary: Take the signed seller half and publish it

get.summary: The message a listing owner signs before managing it

200.description: The challenge to sign with the key that owns the offered output.

post.summary: Remove a listing, proved by the key owning the output it sells
post.description: Withdrawal is discovery, not cancellation. It stops this gateway publishing the listing; it cannot unpublish a signed artifact already distributed elsewhere. Only spending the offered output makes such an artifact unusable.

401.description: Operator credentials missing, invalid, or not configured.

get.summary: The unsigned kind 802 event announcing this listing
get.description: The gateway never holds Nostr keys. The customer's own NIP-07 signer signs this envelope, the browser publishes it, and the signed event can then be handed back through the OpenOrdex import route.

post.summary: Recheck one order against both authorities

201.description: The order after a fresh verification.

post.summary: Compose the buyer half and state the exact terms
post.description: The caller names its own outputs and nothing else. Value and script are read from Bitcoin Core, never from the request, so a buyer cannot make a purchase look cheaper by describing their own funding wrongly. Each named output is checked against the ord index first: an output holding an asset is not spare change, and an unexamined output is unknown rather than empty.

201.description: The unsigned buyer half and the exact economics. A fee or a royalty of zero is stated as zero rather than omitted.

post.summary: Verify a signed purchase and ask the node whether it would accept it
post.description: Takes either `finalTxHex` or the `signedPsbt` a wallet actually answers with. Given a PSBT it finalises only inputs the buyer already signed: it creates no signature and changes no input, output, or amount, and an unsigned input is an error rather than a guess. It rechecks the order against the chain, binds the transaction to the order, proves the sat flow invariant, then asks the node itself. The gateway does not broadcast; that is the buyer's own deliberate step.

201.description: The verdict, with the exact bytes checked so a buyer broadcasts those and no others.

post.summary: Replace a live ask with a freshly signed one for the same output
post.description: Repricing is a protocol operation, not a database edit. The old order must be live, the owner proof must match the offered output, and the new artifact must be signed against the same outpoint. The old order leaves the book as REPLACED and the new one goes live in one step, and two live asks for one output and seller cannot exist.

201.description: The retired order id and the live replacement.

post.summary: Compose several live asks into one transaction
post.description: Up to eight asks, one funding plan, one transaction, composed only when every seller signature and every sat flow invariant can coexist. There is no partial composition: when any ask cannot be proved the answer names every refusal and settles nothing.

201.description: The composed batch with every placement stated.

409.description: At least one ask cannot coexist in the batch.

post.summary: Verify a signed batch and ask the node about the exact bytes
post.description: Rechecks every placement against both authorities, proves the sat flow invariant for every ask, then asks the node whether it would accept the composed transaction. The answer carries the exact bytes checked.

201.description: The per-ask verdicts and the node answer.

get.summary: One page of the offer book
get.description: Keyset paged exactly like the orders: limit and cursor in, nextCursor out, empty on the last page. A malformed cursor is a 400, never a silent first page.

post.description: Takes exact offer terms and funded-output evidence. The gateway recomputes the terms hash, recomputes the Taproot tree and tweak from the two leaves, requires the funded script to commit to both, asks Bitcoin Core whether the output exists and is unspent, and refuses everything else. The offer goes live once the funding confirms.

get.summary: One offer with its lifecycle state and freshness

post.summary: Recheck one offer against both authorities
Remove an offer from discovery, proved by the recovery key
post.description: Discovery, not cancellation: the funded output stays spendable by the acceptance path until it is spent, and by the recovery path after expiry. A BIP 322 signature by the recovery key proves who may stop publishing the offer.

post.summary: State the exact acceptance arrangement for one live offer
post.description: Given the seller outpoint, reads every value from the node and the ord index, lays out padding, buyer asset, every preserve in sat order, the seller payment at the seller input index, and change, and refuses when the Feline is elsewhere, the root no longer holds, or expiry has passed.

201.description: The exact arrangement to build and sign.

post.summary: Verify a built acceptance and ask the node
post.description: Parses the complete acceptance, checks every rule in spec/offers.md including both policy signatures against the committed terms tree, then asks the node whether it would accept the bytes. The answer carries the exact bytes checked.

operatorBasic.description: Operator credentials configured on the gateway. Public routes never require them.

Error.description: The request failed. The envelope states the status, a human readable message, and the request id.

BadRequest.description: The request is malformed or refused, with the exact reason in `message`.

RateLimited.description: Rate limited. The envelope carries `code: ORDEX_RATE_LIMITED`.

AtomicSats.description: An exact non-negative atomic amount as a decimal string. Never floating point, never grouped, never padded.

Source.description: Where order evidence arrived from. Source is provenance, never proof; the node and the ord index decide the state.

OrderState.description: Every state is reachable. A mempool conflict can return to LIVE when the conflicting spend is replaced or dropped; a confirmed spend does not come back short of a reorg. SETTLED is narrower than SPENT: the offered output was spent by a transaction observed carrying this order's exact payout. REPLACED is the terminal state of a live ask whose owner published a fresh ask for the same output through POST /orders/{id}/replace.

Actionability.description: What a customer may do right now. A LIVE order whose verification has aged past its freshness bound is REVIEW_ONLY, not HANDOFF_READY.

inscriptionNumber.description: Read from the local ord index during verification, never from a claim.

Settlement.description: Chain settlement the gateway actually observed, never an assumption.

VerificationView.description: Read-time freshness of the last verification. Age is published with every order so staleness is visible rather than implied.

OrderSummary.description: What a list or detail response carries. The signed artifact is deliberately absent; it is released only through its own rate limited route while the order is live.

sellerScriptHex.description: The output script of the PSBT input being sold. Only the key behind it can have created this listing, so it is the identity every seller management action is checked against.

protocolId.description: User supplied discovery metadata. It never substitutes for chain verification.

nextCursor.description: Keyset resume point for the next page. Empty when this page is last.

hasMore.description: Derived from nextCursor, never from a total that concurrent writes can move.

fromState.description: Null for the first transition an order makes.

actor.description: Who caused the transition: the reconciler, the seller, an operator, or an import.

QuoteRequest.description: What a buyer names when asking the gateway to price a purchase. The buyer names its own outputs and nothing else.

assetReceiveAddress.description: Where the buyer receives the asset. Never the payment address.

paymentAddress.description: Where the buyer's change and merged padding return.

paddingUtxos.description: Outputs placed ahead of the offered one, so the asset reaches the buyer.

Quote.description: Everything a buyer needs to decide, and the unsigned half their wallet will be asked to sign. Every amount is atomic sats as a string.

sellerIndex.description: The index the seller's input and payment output share.

paddingSats.description: Padding the buyer supplies and receives back, so it is not a cost.

PreflightRequest.description: Either the final transaction hex or the signed PSBT a wallet actually answers with.

finalTxHex.description: The exact bytes checked, so a buyer broadcasts those and no others.

psbt.description: The seller half, now signed by the seller's own wallet.

OwnershipChallenge.description: The message a seller signs to prove they own a listing's source UTXO.

ProtocolCapabilities.description: What a protocol can truthfully do today. An entry in the catalog never implies a working flow beyond these booleans.

verifyAssetSemantics.description: True when the local ord index proves the asset's current location, not only that its UTXO is unspent.

verificationScope.description: Plain language scope of what verification proves for this protocol. Never softened to look more capable.

aliasOf.description: Set when this id is a catalog alias of another protocol. Aliases stay filterable but are not offered as a separate market leaf.

ListingReadiness.description: Whether a Bitcoin listing can actually be verified right now. Observed, never inferred from the presence of a URL.

OfferKind.description: What an offer binds to. ITEM names one exact inscription; COLLECTION names every Feline included in the committed root; TRAIT names one exact trait name and value inside that root.

OfferState.description: The funded-output lifecycle. PENDING_CONFIRMATION is not live. ACCEPTED and RECOVERED are the two settled outcomes. EXPIRED means the current height passed expiryHeight with the output unspent, so recovery is the only remaining path. WITHDRAWN is discovery, not cancellation: only a spend settles the funds.

schema.description: The terms schema this contract carries.

protocolVersion.description: The gateway protocol version the terms were written for, 1.1 or later.

collectionRoot.description: Lowercase hex SHA-256 collection Merkle root the scope binds to.

itemInscriptionId.description: ITEM offers only: the exact inscription the offer buys.

traitName.description: TRAIT offers only: the exact trait name.

traitValue.description: TRAIT offers only: the exact trait value.

criteriaHash.description: SHA-256 over the exact serialized scope criteria the buyer accepted, so a verifier can recheck scope membership without trusting a description of it.

buyerReceiveScriptHex.description: Lowercase hex script the bought Feline must land in.

priceSats.description: Exact price paid to the accepting seller.

maxNetworkFeeSats.description: The largest fee an acceptance may pay.

expiryHeight.description: Block height after which acceptance is refused and the recovery path unlocks.

buyerRecoveryKeyHex.description: Lowercase hex x-only key that can recover the funded output alone after expiry.

OfferTermsHash.description: SHA-256 over the terms serialized as UTF-8 JSON with object keys sorted recursively and no insignificant whitespace. Two parties that hold the same terms hold the same hash.

fundedTxid.description: The transaction that created the funded output.

tapInternalKeyHex.description: Lowercase hex x-only internal key of the funded output.

acceptanceLeafScriptHex.description: The acceptance leaf: the terms hash push, both policy keys, CHECKSIG, CHECKSIGADD, and the 2-of-2 equal. The gateway recomputes the tree and the tweak from these leaves, so the funded script must commit to the exact terms.

recoveryLeafScriptHex.description: The recovery leaf: the expiry height, CHECKLOCKTIMEVERIFY, and the buyer recovery key.

checkedAt.description: When both authorities were last asked.

nodeStatus.description: What Bitcoin Core said about the funded output.

rootStatus.description: What the collection authority said about the committed root.

id.description: The gateway identifier for this offer.

settledByTxid.description: ACCEPTED and RECOVERED offers only: the transaction that settled the funds.

acceptedOrderId.description: ACCEPTED offers only: the order whose acceptance carried the settlement.

postedAt.description: When the gateway published the offer.

nextCursor.description: Empty on the last page. Resume from here for a stable, offset-free read.

sellerFelineOutpoint.description: The output the accepting seller will spend to deliver the Feline.

sellerPaymentScriptHex.description: The script the seller payment output must carry, committed by the seller signature.

sellerInputIndex.description: Where the Feline input sits, and with it the seller payment.

offerInputIndex.description: Where the funded offer output sits.

inputs.description: Every input in transaction order, with the exact values read from the node.

outputs.description: Every output in transaction order: padding merge, buyer asset, seller preserves in sat order, seller payment at the seller input index, buyer change last.

estimatedFeeSats.description: The fee the composed arrangement pays at the current rate.

withinMaxNetworkFee.description: False means the terms refuse acceptance as composed.

expiresAtHeight.description: The terms expiry height, restated so a stale plan is visible.

finalTxHex.description: The complete acceptance, seller signature and both policy signatures included.
The exact bytes checked, so a seller broadcasts those and no others.

policySignatureCount.description: How many of the two acceptance-leaf signatures the parsed witness carries.

nodeAcceptance.description: What the node answered when asked whether it would accept these bytes.

ReplaceAskRequest.description: A freshly signed seller half for the same offered output, plus the same owner proof withdrawal requires. The old order leaves the book as REPLACED and the new one goes live in one step.

orderIds.description: The live asks to settle in one transaction, in the order the buyer reviewed them.

assetReceiveAddress.description: Where every purchased Feline lands, one output per ask.

paymentAddress.description: Where padding merges and change return to the buyer.

paddingUtxos.description: Two asset-free cardinal outputs per ask, read back from the node before anything is composed.

fundingUtxos.description: Cardinal outputs that cover every price and the fee.

feeRateSatsPerVb.description: The exact rate the buyer approved.

psbt.description: The unsigned buyer half. Every seller input arrives already signed; the buyer signs only their own inputs.

totalBuyerCostSats.description: Every price, every fee, and every padding sat, stated once.

expiresAt.description: How long the composed batch stays composable before at least one ask can no longer be proved.

code.description: A stable, machine readable refusal code.

reason.description: A human explanation of the same refusal.

BatchPurchaseRefused.description: Answered when at least one ask cannot coexist in the batch. There is no partial composition: every refused order is named, and the client falls back to separate purchases.

batchId.description: The identifier the batch-purchase answer carried.

signedPsbt.description: The batch PSBT with every buyer input signed.

finalTxHex.description: Or the exact final bytes, when already finalized.
The exact bytes checked, so a buyer broadcasts those and no others.

rejectReason.description: Present when this ask failed inside an otherwise parseable batch.

nodeAcceptance.description: What the node answered about the exact composed bytes.

ErrorResponse.description: The error envelope every route answers with. Rate limited requests additionally carry `code: ORDEX_RATE_LIMITED`.
